glossary.Dilation: Widening of a vessel beyond its normal diameter.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue, starving it of oxygen.
glossary.Occlusion: Complete blockage of a vessel so blood cannot pass.
glossary.Perfusion: Delivery of blood through the capillaries of a tissue.
glossary.Pallor: Unusual paleness of the skin from reduced blood flow.
glossary.Paralysis: Loss of the ability to move a muscle; in a limb it signals nerve and muscle ischaemia.
glossary.Pulseless: No palpable pulse distal to a blockage.
glossary.Pulsatile abdominal mass: A lump in the abdomen that throbs with each heartbeat, suggesting an aortic aneurysm.
glossary.Common femoral artery: Main artery of the leg in the groin, continuing from the external iliac artery.
glossary.Deep femoral artery: Branch of the femoral artery (profunda femoris) supplying the thigh muscles.
glossary.External iliac artery: Pelvic artery that becomes the common femoral artery as it passes under the inguinal ligament.
glossary.Popliteal artery: Continuation of the femoral artery behind the knee.
glossary.Cardiac embolism: A clot formed in the heart that travels and lodges in an artery.
glossary.Embolisation: The process of a clot or debris travelling in the blood and blocking a distant vessel.
glossary.Doppler ultrasound: Ultrasound that uses frequency shift to show and measure blood flow.
glossary.DR ABCDE: Danger, Response, Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, Exposure: structured emergency assessment.
glossary.Distal propagation: Extension of a clot further downstream along the vessel.
glossary.Necrosis: Death of cells or tissue from injury or lack of blood supply.
glossary.Stenosis: Abnormal narrowing of a vessel or opening.
glossary.Open repair: Surgical replacement of an aneurysmal artery with a graft through a large incision.
glossary.Revascularisation: Any procedure that restores blood flow to an ischaemic tissue.
glossary.Lifestyle modification: Changes such as stopping smoking, exercise and diet to slow disease.
glossary.Skeletal muscle: Voluntary muscle attached to bone, which tolerates only a few hours without blood.
glossary.Peripheral nerves: Nerves outside the brain and spinal cord, very sensitive to ischaemia.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.Vascular surgery: Surgical specialty treating diseases of the arteries and veins.
